# Source basis

- Experimental `--simt-index-refresh line128` is project-owned code based on the3510 SIMT DCache128B line table and `asc_dcci_single` semantics in official `cann/asc-devkit@50183e8a667c57c10d4ab4e2610872826518f447` (`docs/zh/guide/programming_guide/advanced_programming/memory_model/cache_coherence.md`, `docs/zh/api/SIMT-API/memory_access_functions/asc_dcci_single.md`). Each lane retains full span coverage, including crossings, under the existing stable-request ownership contract; default element mode remains. No fork headers are patched. CPU tracing and VF models are not target cache/performance proof. See `aiv/SIMT_INDEX_REFRESH.md`.

- Optional `--profile-simt` is project-owned scalar-AIV call-envelope timing, reusing the existing completion handshake and a separately allocated128B profile record. It does not modify the pinned fork, lane DCCI, group barriers, CQE contract or communication protocol. The new context layout requires matching Host/AIV builds and native verification; profile-off generated performance is not assumed identical. See `aiv/SIMT_SGL_PROFILE.md`.

- `aiv/launcher.cc` is project-owned Host supervision code using POSIX spawn, owned-PID polling and signal/deadline cleanup. The online worker entry retains the public ACL/HCOMM/resource skeleton but no longer uses the copied example's fork-only `ProcessGroup`; that unchanged helper remains for historical finite probes. Section 38's data/stream success plus overall exit timeout motivates explicit process-boundary evidence, without identifying a specific closed-source SDK finalizer as root cause. CPU lifecycle tests and the separately deduced integer-scalar stubs are project code. See `aiv/HOST_LIFECYCLE.md`.
- Following the section 37 SDK regression, the normal SDK target restores the SIMD compiler settings and UB footprint from verified `49b3c7e4b7c36f01a9aa5a6a1b71a9c07d61bba9`, with the unvalidated SDK SIMT extension behind an explicit disabled-by-default option. SDK and fork Device code now link into different executables. The SIMD builder uses compile-time CQE-policy dispatch; the new CPU model exercises its actual integer/mask operations. Optional phase/mismatch telemetry reuses mailbox padding and adds no communication tasks. These are isolation/diagnostic changes whose native effect remains to be tested, not a confirmed root-cause claim. See `aiv/REGRESSION_DEBUG.md`.
- `aiv/simt_sgl_builder.h` and `transfer_simt_sgl.cpp` integrate the fixed `shao_junyi/asc-comm@14d8b1c3e9037c114bd59f2191e07447c9322a68` SIMT group/multi-source API already validated by the finite probe. Raw Host channel setup follows that probe; the group append/commit and one-source two-half handling follow the fork's `05_simt_urma_perftest/group_perftest_device.h`. The persistent mailbox loop follows this project's verified AIV online service. Actual GM index consumption, lane-side refresh/bounds checks, separate queue snapshots, completion publication and optional per-translation-unit build isolation are project code. `aiv/control.cc` retains its existing protocol. This combined online backend requires its own native verification; finite-probe results do not establish persistent-service correctness or bandwidth. See `aiv/SIMT_SGL.md`.
- `simt_sgl_probe/` isolates the SIMT multi-source extension from [shao_junyi/asc-comm@14d8b1c3e9037c114bd59f2191e07447c9322a68](https://gitcode.com/shao_junyi/asc-comm/tree/14d8b1c3e9037c114bd59f2191e07447c9322a68), branch `simd_sgl_oneCQE`, SGL introduction `23746dd28ab32de1a2b43a232ce8457a82fc52f3`. Its staging script preserves committed header/implementation bytes and license notices inside the build directory. The finite launch, actual-SQ evidence capture and full-pool validation are project code. Host initialization reuses the four existing `aiv/utils/` files below and the fork's `05_simt_urma_perftest` raw-channel setup pattern. The native validation scope and remaining gates are recorded in `simt_sgl_probe/README.md`; the installed SDK's single-source overload remains a separate baseline.
- The probe's `group_kernel.cpp` follows the same fork's `05_simt_urma_perftest/group_perftest_device.h` group append/commit pattern, including its two-half representation for a logical single-source tail in a uniform two-BB batch. The per-request shuffled sources, finite-launch queue-continuity checks, actual-WQE snapshots, full-pool Host verification and CPU VF model are project code. The CPU runner uses the fixed fork's `tests/host/hcomm_simt/host_intrinsics.h` unchanged as temporary CPU substitutes, retaining its notices. The internal report confirms native multi-lane, tail and queue-reuse validation at `7e57e21`; persistent online service and bandwidth remain separate gates. See `simt_sgl_probe/README.md` for scope and evidence.
- `aiv/simt_builder.h` follows `examples/aicore/hcomm/06_simt_hcomm_urma_batch_perf/op_kernel.cpp` at the same `cann/asc-comm@52e478456c7ae6491a172ed0268695c63d21ba56`, using the C25B046 interfaces confirmed by the validation report in section 32. Each cooperative-group lane posts one shuffled 512-byte block, and a persistent AIV entry invokes the VF repeatedly. SIMD's optional per-WQE CQE policy supports the comparison. The SIMT backend's target build and runtime behavior require separate verification.
- `aiv/` adapts the user-supplied, hash-verified `s29_20261119_cachefix` reference probe. Its base is [cann/asc-comm](https://gitcode.com/cann/asc-comm/tree/52e478456c7ae6491a172ed0268695c63d21ba56) at `52e478456c7ae6491a172ed0268695c63d21ba56`, example `examples/aicore/hcomm/02_hcomm_urma_batch_write`. The four files in `aiv/utils/` are unchanged copies of `examples/aicore/utils/{arg_parser,hccl_comm_init,process_manager,rank_sync}.h` from that commit. Copyright and license notices are retained.
- The SIMD encoding in `aiv/vector_builder.h` derives through that probe from [shao_junyi/asc-comm simd_sgl_parallel](https://gitcode.com/shao_junyi/asc-comm/blob/618456a6b4226c740488c53b0f16da76d390ce8c/examples/aicore/hcomm/11_simd_urma_perftest/simd_wqe_builder.h), pinned to `618456a6b4226c740488c53b0f16da76d390ce8c`. The probe added arbitrary-index Gather/Scatter. The external adaptation adds a shared batch plan, bounds/error checks, exact-width mailbox publication, per-request statistics retention, independent scalar/vector options and a separate build/vendor. Source inspection and reference probe execution do not imply verification of this external adaptation. See [aiv/README.md](aiv/README.md).
- [pandeng01/aicpu-comm-ops-examples](https://gitcode.com/pandeng01/aicpu-comm-ops-examples/tree/76fce089b9282d3faedd89bfcf7ce3fd97349424) at `76fce089b9282d3faedd89bfcf7ce3fd97349424`. The CPack/Makeself files under `cmake/` and package installer files under `scripts/custom/` are taken from this snapshot. The CMake target structure and ACL binary load, function resolution, argument and launch sequence follow `hccl_ops/api_coverage`. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
- [CANN cmake](https://gitcode.com/cann/cmake/tree/4fc31230249c6f4edec8bda1bc0110a50347c038) at `4fc31230249c6f4edec8bda1bc0110a50347c038`. It supplies the build and packaging helpers. The Makeself archive is provided separately and verified by the SHA-256 from that snapshot.
- [CANN HCCL Custom P2P](https://gitcode.com/cann/hccl/tree/cd27f581a68329fadc428385af8880f33824d29d/examples/04_custom_ops_p2p) at `cd27f581a68329fadc428385af8880f33824d29d`. Reference for rank-graph UB_CTP selection, thread/stream binding, cross-engine notify and device batch submission. The transfer orchestration here uses a request-list WRITE followed by three payload WRITEs and a receiver acknowledgment.
